steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Choreographic devices are tools used to develop and structure movement material

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Repetition involves repeating a movement or phrase to create emphasis or recognition

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Unison means all dancers performing the same movement at the same time

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Canon is when dancers perform the same movement one after another in sequence

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between unison and canon? | Q: Describe how accumulation works as a choreographic device. | Q: Why might a choreographer use retrograde in a dance?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: In unison, all dancers move at the same time; in canon, dancers start the same phrase at different times in sequence. | Accumulation starts with one movement, then adds a second so both are performed, then a third, and so on — the phrase gradually grows longer with each repetition. | Retrograde creates a striking visual effect, like rewinding time. It can symbolise memory, returning to the past, or give a phrase a surprising twist that maintains audience interest.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name the specific device — do not just describe what happens Link each device to its effect on the audience and the choreographic intention In NEA written tasks, identify the device and explain why you chose it For professional works, identify devices used and explain how they contribute to the piece Remember: devices develop material, they do not replace it — the original movement is always the foundation
